findings.reason: the whole section exists to emit that one verdict, and without a stated μr set and tolerance the verdict is not reproducible, so a node could report "representation implicated" for a solver artefact or "sound" for a 20 % miss.
findings.text: done-when (1) requires the imas-efit shielding factor to be "recorded … against the exact value" and clause (3) requires "the one-directional verdict … written into the plan", but neither names the relative permeability the comparison is made at (the exact S of §1 is μr-dependent: 1.488, 6.902 and 61.10 at μr = 10, 100 and 1000) nor an acceptance tolerance, so any number satisfies clause (1) and either verdict satisfies clause (3); the node cannot fail and two readers can score the same run differently

findings.reason: the verdict is the node's only product, and without a convergence arm on the imas-efit side it would send the §1 hypothesis (and §9's follow-on) in a direction the evidence cannot support.
findings.text: the sentence "if imas-efit misses S, its representation is implicated" attributes a miss to the B-spline boundary-current representation, but nothing in the section requires imas-efit's own discretisation (its knot and observation-point counts, and the `internalResolution` and `responseTolerance` iron-model knobs) to be refined before the verdict is drawn, and imas-efit's iron iteration is configured to stop at `relativeError="1e-2"` (imas-efit `configuration/machines/_common/solver/iron-solver.xml:15`), so a difference of a couple of per cent is inside imas-efit's own solve tolerance and a larger one is equally consistent with a coarse shell; the stated inference is not established by the mechanism as written

findings.reason: the route itself resolves and is correct (iron.xml is included into `efitOptions.xml`, so an authored `<ironBoundaries>` there is read), and the μr = 1 arm fails loudly if the IDS leaks in, so the node corrects the detail in place rather than being sent down a wrong path.
findings.text: the section cites `configuration/machines/WEST/iron.xml` as the "XML `ironBoundaries` fallback", but that file contains only `<include …iron-solver.xml/>` and a single `<magneticPermeabilities relativePermeability="215">`, with no `<ironBoundaries>` element, and `src/tokamakData.cpp:129-137` reads the fallback geometry from the merged tokamakData document only when `imas.hasIronCore()` is false, so the shell geometry must be authored from scratch and the iron_core IDS must be suppressed, which "configured through the XML boundary" does not say

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — all three cited imas-efit anchors resolve (`configuration/machines/WEST/iron.xml`, `src/tokamakData.cpp`, `src/ironCoreBuilder.cpp`), but iron.xml carries no `<ironBoundaries>` element, so the cited file is not the geometry fallback the sentence calls it.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s10's done-when (1) and (3) record a measurement and a verdict with no agreement tolerance and no μr named for the comparison, so "reproduces S" versus "misses S" has no decision rule.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the receipt and the message copy are written under `/work/projects/imas_gpu/sophelio/evidence/iron-core-magnetisation/imas-efit/closed-shell/`, a durable GPFS path of the same family the plan already cites for `magnetics-residuals.json`, and the verdict lands in the plan, which is versioned.

rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s10 delivers one cross-code comparison (the shell result and the WEST probe tabulation are two views of the same imas-efit-versus-nova comparison), with the §6 seam explicitly out of scope.
